deliverables.title: Company profile
deliverables.instr: In the Report Builder, export Cyber Hub 00 as a PDF. It holds your cover page, team agreement and rack sheet.
checks: Communication methods, decisions and missed labs

deliverables.title: Rack sheet
deliverables.instr: Your completed rack sheet, in the same Cyber Hub 00 export.
checks: The rack number you were assigned
Signed off by a teammate and the instructor

deliverables.title: Rack and stack
deliverables.instr: Take a photo of your team holding the server off its rails.
checks: The server is off the rails, held by two people, one on each side

deliverables.title: OOB interface summary
deliverables.instr: Show the switch's interface IP summary in the console window.
checks: The whole console window is visible and uncropped

deliverables.title: Saved configuration
deliverables.instr: Show the startup configuration after saving.
checks: The whole console window is visible and uncropped

deliverables.title: Interface settings
deliverables.instr: Show the firewall's network interfaces list.
checks: wan1, internal and dmz match the table in Part 4

deliverables.title: Static routes
deliverables.instr: Show the static route list, or the routing table from the CLI.

deliverables.title: Provider services
deliverables.instr: Show the firewall CLI pinging your provider's gateway and the lab name server, then the NTP status.

title: Firewall Policies and Guest Wi-Fi
questions: Upstream_Services and DMZ_to_Repo each allow one destination and a few services. Which of your devices will use them, and what would they lose without them?

deliverables.title: Policies and virtual IPs
deliverables.instr: Show the firewall policy table and the virtual IP list.
checks: All seven policies with the services and NAT settings above
All three mappings point into the DMZ

deliverables.title: Guest network lease
deliverables.instr: Show the guest interface's DHCP leases.
checks: The guest laptop has an address in 10.R.50.0/24

deliverables.title: Guest isolation
deliverables.instr: On the guest network, show the laptop's address beside a failed attempt to reach the firewall.

title: Core Switching and VLANs
questions: The plan leaves VLAN 1 unused and puts unused ports in VLAN 999. What could happen if a stray cable were plugged into an unconfigured port otherwise?
Which VLANs get no SVI, and why?
Which next hop did you use for the default route, and why that address?

deliverables.title: Management services
deliverables.instr: Show the TCP/UDP services page.

deliverables.title: VLAN table
deliverables.instr: Show the VLAN table.
checks: Every VLAN in the plan, with matching IDs and names

deliverables.title: VLAN interfaces
deliverables.instr: Show the IPv4 interfaces list.
checks: An SVI for each VLAN the switch routes, matching your rack sheet
No SVI on a VLAN the switch shouldn't route

title: Switch Ports and DHCP
questions: Before you test: if the switch's default route were missing, which row would fail first, and why?
After you test: what does each passing row prove? Explain any result that didn't match your prediction.

deliverables.title: Port settings
deliverables.instr: Show the interface and VLAN membership settings.
checks: XG3 with the right untagged and tagged VLANs
Every other port matches the port map
XG6 to XG8 in VLAN 999 and shut down

deliverables.title: Connectivity checkpoint
deliverables.instr: Show your laptop's address in a terminal beside the firewall login page, loaded from the Data VLAN.
checks: The firewall login page at https://10.R.100.1

title: Network Storage
questions: How many drives can fail before this pool loses data?
What does RAID 5 give up in exchange for that protection?
Your Data laptop can ping the NAS. Can it also open the NAS's login page, and should it be able to?

deliverables.title: NAS discovery
deliverables.instr: Show the DHCP bindings page.

deliverables.title: DSM Info Center
deliverables.instr: Show DSM's Info Center.
checks: The NAS's fixed address from your rack sheet

deliverables.title: NFS permissions
deliverables.instr: Show the NFS service and the share's NFS permissions.
checks: Only the subnets that need the share

deliverables.title: Storage reachability
deliverables.instr: Show a successful ping to the NAS.
checks: A laptop on the Data or Management VLAN

title: Hypervisor and Shared Storage
questions: XG3 is a trunk. Why does vmbr0 have to be VLAN-aware for your VMs to use it?

deliverables.title: Proxmox console
deliverables.instr: Take a photo of the server monitor showing the Proxmox console.
checks: The web interface address on the Management VLAN
The text is sharp and readable

deliverables.title: Bridge and storage
deliverables.instr: Show vmbr0's settings and the Datacenter storage list.

title: DMZ Web Server
questions: If you left the VM's VLAN tag blank, which network would it land on, and why?
For each test, which firewall policy or setting from Cyber Hub 03 makes it work?
The laptop on CyberHub-Internet opens your public name instead of the web server's address. Which address does that name resolve to, and why can't it be the web server's own?

deliverables.title: Web server VM
deliverables.instr: Show the VM's hardware summary.

deliverables.instr: Show your company homepage loaded on a laptop on CyberHub-Internet, with the laptop's address beside it.
checks: Your company homepage with its logo
A terminal shows the laptop's 198.51.100.x address

deliverables.title: Page from the guest Wi-Fi
deliverables.instr: Show your company homepage loaded from a laptop on the guest Wi-Fi.

title: Services and Traffic Analysis
questions: Which settings from Cyber Hub 04 protect the switch's own logins from this kind of capture?

deliverables.instr: Show the VM's hardware summary.

deliverables.instr: Show the install output and the service status.

deliverables.title: Cleartext password

checks: The password is visible in plain text

title: Scanner Appliance
questions: Why give the scanner its own narrow, logged policy instead of widening an existing one?
Which finding on the FTP server matches what you captured in Cyber Hub 09?
Pick one other finding. Is it a real risk for your company, or something you would accept? Why?

deliverables.title: Scanner appliance
deliverables.instr: Show the scanner VM's summary in Proxmox beside Greenbone's feed status.
checks: rackR-scan running, disk on the NFS storage
The last sync date is shown

deliverables.instr: Show Greenbone's results for your Pi.

deliverables.title: Private answer key

checks: All four, each with how it was configured
Exact steps to fix each one

title: Vulnerability Assessment
questions: The WAN scan found open ports even though ping is off. What does that say about hiding a device from ping?
Compare the two views. Which of the target's services can anyone on the internet reach, and which only an insider? Which would you fix first, and why?

deliverables.title: Hosted appliance
deliverables.instr: Show your appliance's web interface, reached from your laptop on the target's Data VLAN.
checks: The appliance's address on the target's Data VLAN

deliverables.title: Network map
deliverables.instr: Show the Nmap results.
checks: Live hosts on the target's Data and DMZ subnets
Open ports and services on the target's WAN address, scanned from CyberHub-Internet

deliverables.title: Scan results
deliverables.instr: Show Greenbone's results summary.

deliverables.title: Assessment in your logs
deliverables.instr: Show the assessment in your firewall's forward traffic log.
checks: Sessions from a 198.51.100.x address on Allow_Inbound_Services

deliverables.title: Vulnerability Assessment Report
deliverables.instr: Export the VAR as a PDF from the Report Builder and submit it before Cyber Hub 13. Then choose Send findings to the client. In Google Drive, share the PDF and the findings file with each member of the target team by name, with general access set to Restricted. They import the findings file into their POA&M.
checks: Shared with the target team's members only
Hosts and subnets assessed, the external and internal views, and the rules of engagement
Each with severity, evidence and validation status

title: Remediation and SSP
questions: Why does closing the FTP finding take more than stopping the service?

deliverables.instr: Show your scan results from Cyber Hubs 10 and 11 next to your new scan.
checks: The findings from your earlier scans
